html:
South Carolina began as the southern part of the English colony of Carolina, on the Atlantic coast of North America. King Charles II granted Carolina to eight Lords Proprietors in 1663, and settlers founded Charles Town in 1670.

Many early settlers came from Barbados and brought its plantation model with them. Rice grown in the coastal swamps became the great crop, worked by Africans brought through the Atlantic slave trade. By the early 1700s enslaved Africans outnumbered free colonists. Charles Town traders also bought and sold Native American captives taken in raids across the Southeast.

That traffic helped spark the Yamasee War of 1715, which nearly destroyed the colony. Soon after, the colonists threw off the proprietors, and the Crown took over; North and South Carolina became separate colonies. In 1739 the Stono Rebellion, the largest slave revolt in the mainland British colonies, led to harsher slave laws. South Carolina joined the revolt against Britain in 1776 and became one of the first states of the United States.
